Title: Source 4: The Real Secret of Washington, D. C. It's not all about politics, and in fact it's an extraordinary city.
Author: by Moiss Naím
Content: Many share the view that the U.S. capital is a dismal¹ place...

A visit to the Library of Congress, the largest library in the world, or to `text(one)` of the many `text(dozens)` of museums in the city can surely open one's mind. Washington has the biggest museum complex in the world (which in `2014` was visited by `text(three)` times as many people as the Louvre²) and the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts offers weekly opera, ballet, and music productions of international caliber...

Here comes the revelation that will likely surprise [many]: The real secret of Washington, D.C., is that it is an extraordinary city. The harsh caricatures with which its critics commonly describe it have little in common with reality. Of course, the U.S. capital is a city where politics [are] important and very visible. And yes, political gridlock and dysfunction are rife. But Washington is much more than that.

For instance, Washington is home to the biggest center for biomedical research in the world, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), with nearly `text(6,000)` scientists; `148` current and former NIH-supported researchers have received Nobel Prizes. The NIH's `text(annual)` budget exceeds `text($30 billion)`, an amount larger than the total budget of many nation states. It is also `text(one)` of the most educated cities in the United States...

[A]nother of Washington's assets is its diversity; more than `text(20 percent)` of the city's population was born outside of the U.S. as of `2011`, with `text(35 percent)` of them coming from Asia, and about `text(half)` (`text(41 percent)`) coming from the Americas.

None of this means that the federal government, Congress, the `text(thousands)` of lobbyists that try to influence both, and the enormous number of media outlets from all over the world that cover political Washington aren't an important part of the city. But they are only `text(one)` part of it and, for a lot of the population, not even the most important part. Many other exceptional characteristics make non-political Washington the exceptional city that it actually is.
